THURSDAY, APRIL 2, 1936
Strong Memorial Auditorium, University of Rochester,
Rochester, New York
The meeting was called to order by Third Vice-President Corcoran at
2:50 P.M.
Oral Chapter Reports were then continued by the senior delegates
present from the following Chapters :
Eta Rho Theta Theta
Tau Omicron Nu
Mu Delta Delta Epsilon Phi
In the absence, due to a conflicting examination period, of active Chapter
delegates from the Zeta Zeta, Brother Roger M. Odium, '29, presented the
report of this Chapter.
The reports of the Lambda and EpsUon Chapters were deferred, owing
to the absence of the delegates from those Chapters.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted to adjourn the
Convention until 10 :00 A.M., Friday, April 3rd.
Convention adjourned at 4:10 P.M.
MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
FRIDAY, APRIL 3, 1936
Strong Memorial Auditorium, University of Rochester,
Rochester, New York
The Convention was caUed to order at 10:53 A.M. by President
Archibald Douglas, Lambda '94.
The Recorder read the minutes of the morning and afternoon sessions
of the previous day.
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed that the minutes of the
afternoon session should be approved as read, but that the approval of the
minutes of the morning session be deferred untU the committee appointments
should be completed.
The Committee on Credentials reported that John N. Moran, '36, and
Llewellyn Plaskett, '37, had presented their credentials as delegates from
the Lambda.
The Oral Report from the Lambda was presented by Brother Moran,
as the senior delegate present.
In the absence of representatives from the Epsilon the report of this
Chapter was again deferred.
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed that the Convention form
Page Six

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
a Committee of the Whole for the purpose of discussing Chapter problems
which had been indicated in the Chapter Reports.
President Douglas appointed Brother R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15,
to act as Chairman of the discussion. Brother Corcoran assumed the
Chairmanship, and an open forum discussion followed.
The discussion of practices of Hell-Week resulted in a general consensus
of opinion to the effect that physical initiations be avoided and that an
attempt be made to emphasize the aims of the Fraternity during this time.
The discussion of scholarship direction within the Chapters showed a
real desire for better scholarship, and many methods of improving the
standard were discussed. No conclusion could be reached because of the
variety of problems presented.
The matter of Chapter histories was brought up, and the delegates
reported the condition of their respective histories as follows :
Completed: Delta, Gamma, Xi, Phi, Beta Beta. The Theta delegates
reported that a short history of the Chapter had been written, and that the
Chapter had been unaware of a need for a new one. The Zeta Zeta
delegate reported that a history had been written recently and would be
brought up to date.
Histories in process of compilation were reported by the Sigma, Kappa,
Upsilon (nearly finished), Mu, Omicron and Epsilon Phi.
The delegates from the Zeta, Lambda, Omega, Pi, Tau, Delta Delta,
Theta Theta and Nu Chapters reported that their Chapters had been
unaware of the need for histories. The delegates from the Psi, Iota, Eta
and EpsUon Chapters reported that little or no progress had been made.
No report was made by the Chi or Rho delegates.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted to adjourn
the Convention until 2:30 P.M., AprU 3rd.
Convention adjourned at 12 :55 P.M.
MINUTES OF THE AFTERNOON SESSION
FRIDAY, APRIL 3, 1936
Strong Memorial Auditorium, University of Rochester,
Rochester, New York
The meeting was called to order by President Douglas at 2:40 P.M.
The Oral Report of the Epsilon Chapter was called for but omitted
because of the absence of delegates from that Chapter.
The Convention was again resolved into an open forum for discussion,
with Brother Corcoran as chairman, as in the Morning Session.
A discussion of rushing practices followed. The problems discussed
were too varied for any definite conclusions to be drawn.
The Committee on Credentials reported that Jack H. Davis, '36, had
presented his credentials as delegate from the Epsilon Chapter.
Brother Davis gave a very fine oral report of the Epsilon Chapter.

Brother George R. Cory, Jr., Theta '34, Editor of the Diamond, re
ported on the Diamond. He stated that, as a result of the questionnaire
recently published more alumni and undergraduate news is to be printed.
This will necessitate the publication of Chapter communications in each
issue, instead of twice yearly as heretofore, and the delegates were requested
to urge their Chapter Associate Editors to cooperate.
The problem of legacies was discussed, and the need for acknowledg
ment of letters from alumni concerning legacies was pointed out.
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed that the Convention return
to the regular order of business.
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed that the Convention
adjourn until 10:00 A.M., April 4, 1936.
Convention adjourned at 4:40 P.M.

cepted as read.
The Minutes of the Afternoon Session of April 3rd were read. Re
commendation was made from the Chair that these Minutes be approved
pending abbreviation of the remarks concerning Chapter histories.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, these Minutes were
accepted as corrected.
The report of the Committee to Nominate Members of the Executive
Council was read.
Brother Arthur G. Campbell, Epsilon Phi '38, as Chairman of the
Committee on Nomination of Members of the Executive Council, presented
the following nominations :
Brother Archibald Douglas, Lambda '94, to succeed Brother Charles P.
Spooner, Rho '94, resigned, for a term of one year.
Brother Walter T. Collins, Iota '03, to succeed himself for the usual
term of five years.
Brother Scott Turner, Phi '02, for the usual term of five years.
Brother Frederick Fales, Gamma '96, for the usual term of five years.
Brother Stephen G. Kent, Delta Delta '11, Lambda '14, took the Chair,
since Brother Douglas was a candidate for election.
There being no other nominations, motion was made, seconded and

President Douglas resumed the Chair.
The report of the Committee on Unfinished Business was read.
The report included the question of distributing the expense of delegates
from distant Chapters. Reference was made to the Records of the Con
vention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity in 1935, page 11, paragraph 10, and
it was decided that local alumni should be asked to help meet the expenses
of these delegates, and that the Executive CouncU should take this matter
up with the proper alumni bodies.
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed to lay this motion on the
table.
The Committee on New Business, through Brother James W. WeUs,

No. 1. Resolved: That the delegates and members of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity assembled in Convention in its I03rd year as guests of the
UpsUon Chapter on April 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, 1936, extend their hearty thanks

hospitality to the delegates and other members attending the Convention.
No. 2. Resolved: That the 1937 Convention be held with the Iota

No. 3. Resolved: That we hereby acknowledge our indebtedness to the

No. 4. Resolved: That the Recorder be instructed to write a letter to

The time of the next Convention was discussed. It was decided that

The Committee on Annual Communications presented its report, and

That the Diamond should print more write-ups of famous Psi U active

That the Houses should give more complete Chapter communications.

That the Diamond should contain more information as to how the

Appendix A
THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
TO THE
1936 CONVENTION OF PSI UPSILON
HELD UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL and the UPSILON CHAPTER
Rochester, New York
April 2, 3 and 4, 1936
To the Delegates from our twenty-seven Chapters to this Convention
held in the 103rd Year of our Fraternity, the Executive Council extends a
hearty and Fraternal welcome.
At the beginning of this communication, we would like to pause mo
mentarily and urge that we all reflect on the inherent qualities which must
be deeply embedded in Psi Upsilon when such a social institution of the
American Continent is now in its second century of continued, vigorous
existence. Surely, ours is a noble heritage and an equally great
responsibility.
The Upsilon Chapter, their Alumni Association and the Psi Upsilon
Alumni Association of Western New York have made attractive arrange
ments for this Convention, and all of us present are indebted to them for
their generosity and fine spirit. This is the first time the Fraternity has
met here in convention since the memorable gathering of 1908.
At this Convention, we welcome for the first time the delegates from
our new Chapter, Zeta Zeta. We extend to them a particularly warm
welcome and congratulate them upon achieving their goal in obtaining
their charter. As the newest link in our chain of chapters, they now not
only enjoy equal privileges, but equal responsibflities. The Executive
Council congratulates the Fraternity on its new Chapter; its instaUation
last October was a noteworthy occasion in the history of our Fraternity.
In our communication last year, the Executive Council attempted to
set forth some of the ideals of Psi Upsilon, and we believe that it is of
sufficient importance to repeat that statement again this year:
"Psi Upsilon's fundamental ideal has always been to choose for
its membership the best men it could find and then to make them better,
finer comrades, truer friends, worthier men. That ideal is attested by
the great men who have worn and today wear our badge ; and, equally,
by those other brothers, less noted and much more
numerous, whose
Page Fourteen

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
lives that ideal has made better and more complete. For over a
hundred years, Psi Upsilon has striven to represent the best in American
College life. We are proud of our college record, proud of our
brothers; but if we remain static and rest on our pride in the past, we
shall be false to our ideal of development. Nor should we concern
ourselves too much with reflections on our prosperity and merit. A
great fraternity, if it would remain great, must think more and more
of its opportunity for service to its members and to the college world."
The Year's Accomplishments:
It is the definite opinion of the Executive Council that our Fraternity
never was in better condition as to finances, scholarship, morale and keen
appreciation of the ideals and value of Psi UpsUon than now. Only two or
three chapters have not yet attained a position of creditable scholarship
ranking. We wish to felicitate the Brothers of our Chapters on their
current year's achievements and at the same time urge them to realize that
our splendid standards demand that there be no let-up in their efforts to
meet our ideals.
It is well to recall that within the past two years the fraternity
situation in some of our colleges and fraternities were weighed in the
balance and some fraternity chapters were found wanting. Our Chapters
have an obligation which we choose to express, "Your first obligation is
to your Alma Mater." In this we are content, because we have always
experienced deep loyalty to our Fraternity by a Chapter whose record of
accomplishment and loyalty to its Alma Mater was complete.
Petitions :
This communication is novel in one way. For once, we have nobody
petitioning for a chapter of Psi Upsilon, and in this situation we do not feel
slighted in the least.
Chapter Visits:

Finances of Psi Upsilon:
During the difficult years of the depression, the finances of Psi Upsilon
Page Fifteen

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
nationaUy have been carried through satisfactorily. Our Executive CouncU
has an able Treasurer who is a member of one of the largest banking
firms in the country, and our accounts and investments are in good shape.
Our annual tax of four dollars per year per undergraduate is stiU the
lowest tax of any fraternity in the country.
In order that the Executive CouncU may be in a position to better
fulfill its obligations to the Fraternity as a whole, and in order to enable
us to properly supervise and report on our Chapters' finances, we ask the
Convention to adopt a resolution requiring each Chapter to make a complete
financial statement once a year at the call of the Executive CouncU.
Chapter Histories :
We ask a further resolution that all Chapter Histories be completed
and sent to Brother Albert C. Jacobs, Phi '21, not later than the date set
for the 1937 Convention. We have been urging the Chapters to write their
histories for the past several years. About a third of the Chapters have
them completed. Another third have them in course of preparation, and
we are afraid that the balance have been neglectful of this important
responsibility. The Alumni Associations of the several chapters are urged
to follow up their chapters, as we must not fall down in publishing Volume
II of our epitome.
The Diamond:
The Diamond has proven itself a most valuable medium of keeping
the Brothers in touch with one another, and the members of the Executive
Council together with the officers of Psi Upsflon Alumni Association are
now attempting to secure increased life subscriptions from among our
alumni in order to improve our endowment fund for the magazine, and,
what is more important, to bring the Diamond to an increasing number of
alumni. We trust that the active chapters will lend us assistance in
securing life subscriptions from among alumni in classes prior to 1926.
Badges:
Another recommendation which the Executive CouncU desires to make
to this Convention is the consideration of a resolution that there be only
two official badges hereafter recognized by the Fraternity�
namely, the
official fuH-size badge which each brother receives upon his initiation, and
the official watch charm. The remaining styles of badges of any size or
any other insignia in jewelry shall not be recognized or permitted by the
Fraternity.
In connection with a discussion of our badges, we would feel it incum
bent upon us to refresh your memories that our Constitution provides that
no one except members of the Society are permitted to wear our insignia.
Chapter Group Meetings:
A further recommendation by the Executive CouncU to this Convention
is that the various Chapters hold territorial group meetings such as that

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
held last December at Pi Chapter House. On that occasion, the majority
of undergraduate members of the Pi, Chi, Theta, Upsilon and Psi Chapters
held a one-day informal meeting and get-together, and doubtless the dele
gates of those Chapters wUl relate their reactions. The Secretary of the
Executive Council has written to all of the Chapters suggesting various
geographical groups which could follow the example set by our Northern
New York Chapters, and he has urged that one chapter in each of the
designated groups call together those in its immediate locality.
In no wise do we urge a practice of district conventions, but we would
like to see these informal gatherings become a regular custom in the
Fraternity, as it is a most productive means of obtaining helpful suggestions
for each of the chapters, and it serves as an inspiration to greater achieve
ment and brings about better cooperation in the important matter of secur
ing new members. Fundamentally, it also allows for the development of
a broader and more intimate fellowship among the members of the nearby
chapters; many lasting and delightful friendships are bound to ensue.
Elections to the Executive Council :
The Council caUs to the attention of the Convention the fact that the
terms of Brother Walter T. Collins, Iota '03 and Archibald Douglas,
Lambda '94, expire with this Convention. Since the last convention, the
Council has received with regret the resignation of Charles P. Spooner,
Rho '94, and in accordance with our Constitutional provisions, the Council
has elected to his place Brother Scott Turner, Phi '02.
In accordance with the amendment to our Constitution, passed in 1932,
enlarging the membership of the Council from ten to fifteen (by adding
one additional member for each of five successive years) one additional
member should be elected to the Executive Council to complete the number
on the Council.
In accordance with the Constitution and tradition of the Fraternity, it
is therefore incumbent upon this Convention to elect three brothers to
serve on the Executive CouncU for the usual term of five years each and
to confirm the appointment of Brother Scott Turner to succeed Brother
Charles P. Spooner, his term expiring in 1937.
Psi Upsilon Alumni Association :
The Executive Council would indeed be remiss if it did not commend
to your attention the definite progress being made in the development of
the Psi Upsilon Alumni Association. Brother Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21,
and his brother officers and members of his Board of Governors have
worked quietly and faithfully in their desire to assist the undergraduates
as well as the graduate members of the Fraternity in every way possible.
Definitely, they have been real factors in inspiring our undergraduate
members to higher scholarly achievement through providing awards to all
members of the Fraternity who are elected to the honorary scholastic societies
of Phi Beta Kappa, Tau Beta Pi and Sigma Xi. From their modest income,
the Alumni Association has also awarded this year for the second time an

official Psi Upsilon watch chain charm to one member of the junior
delegation of each chapter who has been selected by his own chapter, as
having contributed most to his chapter during the period of his membership.
The Alumni Association has encouraged the strengthening of existing
alumni clubs situated about the country and been instrumental in the forma
tion of new geographical associations. In no wise, have they interfered
with the normal functioning of the alumni associations of our several
chapters.
We, therefore, respectfully urge our undergraduate members to become
voluntary dues-paying members of the Alumni Association upon their grad
uation. Theoretically, every member of the Fraternity automatically becomes
a member of the Alumni Association after leaving college, and the voluntary
dues of two dollars per year may be paid by those desiring to do so. A
greater income through more paying voluntary dues wUl enable the Alumni
Association to obtain greater accomplishments in their desire to serve the
Fraternity.
1937 Convention:
It will be the duty of this Convention to fix the meeting place for the
1937 Convention. According to rotation provided for in the Constitution,
the next convention should be held with the Iota Chapter at Kenyon College
unless this Convention orders otherwise. The last convention was held at
the Iota in 1910.

Report of the Treasurer
1936
There is presented herewith a comparative statement of the Net Worth
of the various funds of the Fraternity held by the Executive Council as of
AprU 30, 1936 and AprU 23, 1935. A list of the investments held by the
General Fund and Bridgman Fund, showing cost and present market value,
is also presented.
It is to be noted that the cash position as of AprU 30, 1936, showed
considerable improvement. This was due principally to the excess of
income over expenses and to the collection of receivables during the year,
and to a small extent to sales of Directories, Song Books and Song Records.
In comparing the figures of Net Worth as of AprU 30, 1936, with those
a year earlier, it should be noted that total cash increased $2,165.25,
receivables were collected, investments carried at cost increased $1,008.70,
and total net worth increased $1,816.80. The unrealized loss on the securi
ties held in the two investment funds was $6,990.73 as of AprU 30, 1936,
compared with $10,477.53 a year previous, this decrease being due mainly
to the general recovery of the security market during the year. If the
investments were carried in the statement at market value instead of at
cost, the Net Worth of the various funds would work out as $37,169.53
as of April 30, 1936 and $30,865.93 as of April 23, 1935.
The income and expense accounts of the various funds are selfexplanatory. The expenses of the Council in reference to the installation
of the Zeta Zeta Chapter at the University of British Columbia amounted
to $440.66, which were paid out of the General Fund. The Diamond Fund
showed a surplus for the year of $684.39, compared with a loss of $617.41
in the preceding year, due in large part to the success of concerted efforts
to get the cost of printing reduced.
The Treasurer wishes to reiterate that every effort is being made to
